newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller refuses to discuss coalition.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller refuses to discuss coalition.

text.p: Turkish conservative leader Tansu Ciller said on Tuesday she had refused to discuss a planned secularist pact in talks with prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz.

"I did not discuss the government issue, so as not to legitimise Yilmaz's position," Deputy Prime Minister Ciller told reporters after 20 minutes of talks with Yilmaz, a bitter rival for leadership of the Turkish right.
"We said to Yilmaz, 'Go immediately and return the mandate to the president,'" Ciller said. President Suleyman Demirel on Friday asked Yilmaz to form a government.

Yilmaz is almost assured of the support of two left-wing parties, a right-wing grouping and conservative independents but he is still around a dozen votes short of the simple majority he would need to win a confidence vote.

Outgoing Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan, who quit last week after frequent disputes with the army over religious activism, backs a pro-Islamist alliance headed by Ciller, who has served as Erbakan's coalition partner for the last year.
Turkish shares tumbled five percent on Tuesday, eroding more than half of the gains a day earlier, as hopes of a secularist coalition began to crumble.
